extracted.intended_audience: educated early-18th-century English readers / polite society (general readership of The Spectator), with particular address to women and persons interested in manners, language, and moral conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Short moral and satirical essays offering advice and judgments on private conduct, public manners, language usage, devotional reading, and the duties of sexes in polite society. The pieces mix anecdote, letter-form, and rhetorical example to argue norms of behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise weightier excellencies
rubrics_metrics.description: All that I contend for is, that those Excellencies, which are to be regarded but in the second Place, should not precede more weighty Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place substantial, moral, or lasting qualities before lesser pleasures or superficial excellencies. Avoid allowing trifling attractions (beauty, fashionable amusements) to overshadow duties or virtues; do not let secondary delights 'precede more weighty Considerations.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate the mind by instruction to resist illusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If we grant an Equality in the Faculties of both Sexes, the Minds of Women are less cultivated with Precepts, and consequently may... be accounted more liable to Illusion in Cases wherein natural Inclination is out of the Interests of Virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral and intellectual education (precepts) should be used to form habits that prevent being misled by passion or appearances. Instruction that becomes habitual will make right conduct feel instinctive rather than merely performative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love laudable things, not merely avoid vice
rubrics_metrics.description: What is wanting among Women, as well as among Men, is the Love of laudable Things, and not to rest only in the Forbearance of such as are Reproachful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virtue is active: cultivate a positive affection for praiseworthy pursuits rather than defining virtue solely as absence of wrongdoing. Antipattern: claiming virtue by simply avoiding visible vice or performing outward rites without inward commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose devotional books that elevate the mind
rubrics_metrics.description: When you are upon this Subject, choose Books which elevate the Mind above the World, and give a pleasing Indifference to little things in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select religious/devotional writings that promote inward improvement and genuine morality rather than 'weekly preparations' or 'limited Godliness' that produce mechanical religion. Examples/antipatterns: ladies who read many prayer-books in a ritualised way while remaining vain or indulging in vice; devotional practice as an empty show (praying mechanically, then returning to cards until 2–3 a.m.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mechanical religion and empty shows of piety
rubrics_metrics.description: For want of such Instructions, I am apt to believe so many People take it in their Heads to be sullen, cross and angry, under pretence of being abstracted from the Affairs of this Life... All these Acts are but empty Shows, and, as it were, Compliments made to Virtue; the Mind is all the while untouched with any true Pleasure in the Pursuit of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True religion/virtue should touch the mind and produce inward change; beware of routines that serve as social signalling rather than moral transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Female virtues are domestick; avoid partisan zeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Female Virtues are of a Domestick Turn. The Family is the proper Province for Private Women to shine in... as tender Mothers, and faithful Wives, rather than as furious Partizans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise women to excel in home-centered virtues (modesty, maternal fidelity) and to avoid becoming zealous political partisans within domestic or local social circles. If women engage publicly, direct zeal against true public enemies rather than intramural factionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspire to modest, sex-appropriate virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspire only to those Virtues that are peculiar to your Sex; follow your natural Modesty, and think it your greatest Commendation not to be talked of one way or other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value modesty and avoiding public notoriety as central female virtues (invokes Pericles' advice). Antipattern: seeking to be 'talked of' or notorious as a sign of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use learning in public life, not only in recluse study
rubrics_metrics.description: When Learning irradiates common Life, it is then in its highest Use and Perfection; and it is to such as Your Lordship, that the Sciences owe the Esteem which they have with the active Part of Mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly knowledge is most valuable when applied to public/business life to help others; avoid hoarding learning in seclusion where it serves only private ends. Example: a man of business using learning as a torch to guide the bewildered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settle titles and public mistakes in proper season
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of great Consequence to clear Titles, and it is of Importance that it be done in the proper Season... This Affair will be best adjusted in your Life-time; but I hope your Affection to your MOTHER will not make you partial to your AUNT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct public records, attributions, and historical claims while parties are alive to prevent later disputes among critics and chroniclers. Ensure clarity of provenance to avoid future interpolation or contested origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of rivalry and vanity in dress and display
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no end of Affection taken in at the Eyes only; and you may as well satisfie those Eyes with seeing, as controul any Passion received by them only... Their Nights grew restless with Meditation of new Dresses to outvie each other, and inventing new Devices to recal Admirers...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portraits of social rivalry show the moral cost of seeking superiority by display: leads to misery, damaged relationships, and excessive expenditure. Antipatterns: mothers encouraging daughters' expense and gaudy public exhibitions; perpetual attempts to outshine rivals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character revealed by behaviour in both riches and poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: It was the same Baseness of Spirit which worked in his Behaviour in both Fortunes: The same little Mind was insolent in Riches, and shameless in Poverty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reliable test of character is consistent conduct across changing fortune; avoid attributing moral change solely to circumstance—persistent baseness shows through in both wealth and want.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical defence of useful idioms and particles in speech
rubrics_metrics.description: I am not against reforming the Corruptions of Speech You mention, and own there are proper Seasons for the Introduction of other Words besides THAT; but I scorn as much to supply the Place of a WHO or a WHICH at every Turn, as they are unequal always to fill mine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defend flexible, idiomatic usage (e.g., 'that', expletive phrases like 'that is', 'that is to say') as useful rhetorical and discursive tools; do not impose pedantic replacements that make speech awkward. Examples: rhetorical 'That is', 'Such Things as That', and 'Egad and all That' as effective spoken/dramatic speech.
